articles.title: Kacey Musgraves remembers Dolly Parton: Reveals that one habit she broke for the country music icon
articles.summary: Kacey Musgraves reminisces about her encounters with the late Dolly Parton, sharing how the country music icon inspired her to break her habit of being late and the collective grief felt after her passing.
articles.body: Kacey Musgraves recently looked back on her memories of country music legend Dolly Parton, recalling the warmth, humour and humility that made the singer so beloved. Although the two crossed paths several times at award shows and industry events, Musgraves admits that meeting someone she admired so much never stopped feeling special.According to People, Musgraves reflected on her encounters with Parton and revealed that the legendary singer even inspired her to break one of her habits: being late. The Grammy-winning artist also spoke about the collective sadness following Parton's passing in August 2026.Kacey Musgraves recalls meeting Dolly PartonMusgraves, 38, said, “I was lucky to get to be around her several times, and each time I was just like, ‘What do I say?’ Looking back, she described those meetings as memorable experiences that left a lasting impression.The two singers also shared a musical connection. In 2019, Musgraves joined Katy Perry for a performance of Parton's hit 'Here You Come Again' at the MusiCares Person of the Year tribute, which celebrated Parton's contribution to music. Later, Musgraves and Perry joined Parton onstage during the Grammy Awards.“She was exactly like you would think that she would be — so humble, sense of humour, fun, so professional, really warm,” Musgraves said before adding, “You could see someone like that and understand how they could be closed off and jaded, but she was anything but that.”The one habit Kacey Musgraves broke for Dolly PartonOne of the lighter memories Musgraves shared involved her reputation for running late. The singer has previously joked about her poor punctuality through the lyrics of her 2018 song 'Slow Burn', in which she describes herself as someone who is always in a hurry and rarely early.However, meeting Parton was apparently enough to change that routine. Musgraves recalled making a special effort to arrive on time whenever she had an engagement involving the country legend.“I think the only time I’ve probably ever been really, really on time in my life was doing something with Dolly. I was like, ‘I’m not being late for that!’” quipped Musgraves.Kacey Musgraves reflects on the loss of Dolly PartonDolly Parton passed away at 80. Her family announced on August 25, 2026, that she passed away in Nashville following a short battle with cancer.Musgraves later mourned her loss on social media. She also paid tribute through music, performing Parton's songs, including 'Here You Come Again' and '9 to 5', during her 'Middle of Nowhere' tour. At the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards, she honoured the late singer with a performance of 'I Will Always Love You' during the in memoriam segment.“I think losing Dolly was collective grief. And it really, I think, showed us how starved we are for a really true matriarch in that sense. She’s been with us for so long. She’s almost like Mr. Rogers, but times a billion in a way — Mr. Rogers wearing rhinestones. It was amazing to see how beloved she was and, I think, probably the closest thing we have to American royalty, you know what I mean?” Musgraves said.Musgraves also described Parton as one of the closest figures to American royalty because of the affection people across different backgrounds felt for her.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.summary: Fans waiting to see Nazriya Nazim and Fahadh Faasil share screen space again have a reason to be excited.
articles.body: Fans waiting to see Nazriya Nazim and Fahadh Faasil share screen space again have a reason to be excited. The actor has expressed her wish to reunite with her husband for another film and said she is looking forward to finding the right story. Her response has raised hopes among fans, who have been waiting for the popular couple to work together again.Nazriya says she is manifesting a film with Fahadh FaasilSpeaking at the success meet of Suriya's 'Scene' in Kochi, Nazriya was asked whether audiences could expect her and Fahadh to act together in a film. She responded positively and said, "Yes, you should expect it. I also really want to do a film with him. Let a good story come along. It will happen. All of you, please pray for it. I am manifesting it." Her cheerful response has added to the excitement surrounding a possible reunion. However, the actor did not reveal any details about a project or filmmaker who could bring them together.Nazriya and Fahadh Faasil's last film together was 'Trance'The couple was last seen together in director Anwar Rasheed's Trance, which was released in 2020. Before that, they shared screen space in the 2014 Malayalam film 'Bangalore Days,' directed by Anjali Menon. Both films received a good response, and their on-screen chemistry became a favourite among audiences. Although Nazriya and Fahadh have continued to work on separate projects since then, they have not reunited for another film. The couple, who got married in 2014, remain one of the most loved pairs in Malayalam cinema, making Nazriya's latest statement particularly exciting for fans.Nazriya wins praise for her performance in Suriya's Scene'Meanwhile, Nazriya has been receiving attention for her performance in 'Scene,' which stars Suriya in the lead role. In fact, her expressions, action sequence, and screen presence have become talking points among movie buffs. Some social media personalities have appreciated her come back into Tamil films. This is one of the movies where she is making a huge comeback into Tamil cinema through a lead role.
